speakers: Choong Tze Chua (Singapore Management University, Lee Kong Chian School of Business)
summary: Can an arbitrage-free structural forward-curve model (unconditional + maturity-specific habitat + date-specific expectation components, Kalman-filtered) forecast Eurodollar forward rates better than a random walk, and can the forecasts be traded? Method: AIC-select a 6-state model on 1981-1991 data, then expanding-window out-of-sample forecasts 1991-2008 at 5/20/65/250 days. Result: RMSE lower than random walk at every horizon but not significant; trade signals earn positive mean profit (1.19 to 49.04 bp per trade) but nearly equal to always-long futures buy-and-hold.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: a three-part functional decomposition of the forward rate: a long-term, unconditional component, a maturity-specific component, and a date-specific component.
claims.claim: Forward rate = unconditional curve + maturity-specific deviation + date-specific deviation.
claims.exact_rule: F(tau;t)=U(tau)+M(tau;t)+D(tau;t)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The maturity-specific component captures preferred investment habitats, and the date-specific component captures shocks to expectations of future spot rates.
claims.claim: M reflects preferred-habitat supply/demand at specific maturities; D reflects changing expectations of future spot rates.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We demonstrate the use of this approach by fitting this model to yields over the period 12/9/1981 to 1/28/2008. The estimation is accomplished by using a Kalman filter
claims.claim: Sample is 9 Dec 1981 to 28 Jan 2008; states estimated by Kalman filter.
claims.exact_rule: Kalman filter, quasi-ML
claims.data_needed: CME Eurodollar futures settlement prices 1981-12-09 to 2008-01-28

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The estimated yield curve provides better out-of-sample predictions than the standard random walk model in forecasts over various horizons.
claims.claim: Abstract claims better out-of-sample forecasts than the random walk (but Table 3 differences are not significant).
claims.reported_result: RMSE lower at all horizons; NW-stats -0.37 to -1.03, not significant (Table 3)
claims.conditions: the claim of 'better' is not statistically significant

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We further show the profitability of a trading scheme that chooses futures positions based upon the anticipated forward curve.
claims.claim: A trading scheme using forecast direction of forward rates is profitable on average.
claims.reported_result: mean profit 1.19 to 49.04 bp per trade across 5 to 250 day holds

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: An important characteristic that guides the choice from among these alternatives is the ability of the model to forecast forward rates or futures prices.
claims.claim: Authors judge term-structure models by out-of-sample forecast ability.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: CFRS empirically select and estimate a member of this class using a sample of observed “training” data. The resulting model gave good out-of-sample forecasts of US Treasury yields when compared to several extant models that include the random walk model.
claims.claim: Prior paper (Chua, Foster, Ramaswamy, Stine 2008, RFS) forecast US Treasury yields well out-of-sample versus competitors incl. random walk.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: 1. An unconditional curve that represents the steady-state forward curve;
claims.claim: Component 1: unconditional steady-state forward curve.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: 2. A maturity-specific curve that embeds the influence of supply and demand from agents who have needs for loans of specific terms; and
claims.claim: Component 2: maturity-specific curve from supply and demand of agents with term-specific loan needs.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: 3. A date-specific curve that embeds expectations about spot rates to prevail at fixed future dates.
claims.claim: Component 3: date-specific curve holding expectations about spot rates at fixed future dates.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: expectations of future spot rates play no role in this component.
claims.claim: In preferred-habitat deviations expectations of future spot rates play no role; they reflect maturity preferences only (Modigliani-Sutch 1966).

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The date-specific curve embeds all of the information that investors have regarding the levels of future spot rates and summarizes the effects of fundamental monetary influences on expected future interest rates.
claims.claim: Date-specific curve holds all investor information on future spot rates, including monetary influences.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The curve of date-specific deviations corresponds to the influences of the expectations hypothesis.
claims.claim: D corresponds to the expectations hypothesis; M corresponds to deviations from steady state in CIR/Vasicek equilibrium models.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The model has the additional advantage of being demonstrably arbitrage-free.
claims.claim: The model class is arbitrage-free (HJM-verified), unlike simple curve-fitting forecasts.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Our objective here is to show that a representative member chosen from this class of models is able forecast 90-day forward rates to prevail at future dates.
claims.claim: Test target: forecast 90-day forward rates at future dates using a representative member of the model class.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: In the actual estimation we use Eurodollar futures contracts to impute the forward rates.
claims.claim: Forward rates are imputed from Eurodollar futures (liquid, rich data) rather than Treasury yields.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The Eurodollar futures market settles to the rate on dollar-denominated inter-bank loans in London and therefore is affected by a credit risk;
claims.claim: Footnote 1: the model ignores default but Eurodollar futures settle to LIBOR, which carries credit risk.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We first select a member of the CFRS class using the Akaike information criterion over an initial set of training data;
claims.claim: Model selected by AIC on a training sample, then rolled forward and compared to the random walk on a hold-out sample.
claims.exact_rule: AIC model selection on initial training data, parameters estimated there, then out-of-sample comparison

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Our results indicate that the model is useful, most notably at longer forecast horizons.
claims.claim: Authors conclude usefulness grows with horizon.
claims.reported_result: RMSE gap 0.02 bp (5d) to 6.31 bp (250d)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: F (τ ; t) = U (τ ) + M (τ ; t) + D(τ ; t)
claims.claim: Model equation (1): forward rate at time-to-maturity tau = unconditional + maturity-specific + date-specific.
claims.exact_rule: F(tau;t)=U(tau)+M(tau;t)+D(tau;t), tau>0 time to forward start

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: This unconditional curve can be written:
claims.claim: Unconditional curve U(tau)=lim_{s->inf} E_t[F(tau;s)] (Eq 2): the expected forward curve in the distant future, so present information is of little use.
claims.exact_rule: U(tau)=lim s->inf E_t[F(tau;s)]; time-invariant

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The unconditional curve is time invariant and may be estimated by taking an average of all available historical curves.
claims.claim: U is estimated as the average of all historical curves (time invariant).
claims.exact_rule: U(tau) = historical average of F(tau;.) (in the final model: parametric fit to all data up to T, see C16)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: That model postulates that some market participants are primarily concerned with their natural maturity habitat, with little regard for the implication of the forward rates on future spot rates.
claims.claim: Preferred-habitat theory (Modigliani-Sutch): some participants care about their natural maturity and ignore the spot-rate implications of forwards.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The actions of participants with preferred habi- tats affect only those maturities (and nearby maturities) of the forward curve rather than move progressively towards shorter maturities and eventually affect the spot rates.
claims.claim: Habitat effects stay local to a maturity region, they do not roll down toward spot, so they decay rather than shift.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We model the maturity-specific curve as a point-wise mean-reverting process that reverts to zero at a constant rate, so that
claims.claim: M mean-reverts pointwise to zero: E_t[M(tau;T)]=exp(-Km (T-t)) M(tau;t) (Eq 3), Km>0.
claims.exact_rule: E_t[M(tau;T)] = exp(-Km*(T-t)) * M(tau;t) for each fixed maturity tau; Km estimated

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The arbitrage-free formulation of the overall curve of maturity-specific deviations has the property that M (∞; t) = 0 for all t.
claims.claim: Boundary conditions: M(inf;t)=0 and M(0;t)=0 so spot-rate dynamics sit in D.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The concept of a date-specific deviation has its roots from the Expectations Hypothesis (Fisher (1896)).
claims.claim: Date-specific deviation derives from the Expectations Hypothesis (Fisher).

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Therefore a high forward rate today should naturally point towards a higher spot rate at the corresponding date in the future.
claims.claim: Intuition: a high forward rate signals a higher future spot rate at that date.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: In empirical tests, forecasts of forward rates generated by the Expectations Hypothesis model are generally inferior to even the most basic benchmark, the random walk.
claims.claim: Empirically EH forecasts are generally worse than a random walk, so only part of the forward curve is treated as expectation.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The model proposed here attributes only a part of the current forward curve as containing information about future spot rates.
claims.claim: Only the date-specific part of the forward curve is read as information about future spots.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Cox, Ingersoll and Ross (1981) show that some versions of the Expectations Hypothesis admit arbitrage.
claims.claim: CIR (1981): some versions of the EH admit arbitrage; later work (McCulloch, Fisher-Gilles, Longstaff) shows other forms can be consistent with no-arbitrage (footnote 2).

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Treasury needs new additional financing on (or around) s ≡ January 2009. This borrowing will drive up interest rates during that period.
claims.claim: Example: news of Treasury financing needs in January 2009 raises the 1-year forward rate around that date (date-specific shock).
claims.direction: forward rate at maturity date rises

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: E t [D(s − T ; T )] = D(s − t; t)
claims.claim: Date-specific deviation is attached to a calendar date: its expected value at that date is unchanged, so the curve shifts left in maturity as time passes (Eq 5).
claims.exact_rule: E_t[D(s-T;T)] = D(s-t;t), t<T<s

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: At infinite maturity, the date- specific deviation must be zero because it is not plausible that one can have any information about the spot rate in the infinite future
claims.claim: D(inf;t)=0, and D(0;t)=spot rate minus unconditional spot rate.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The maturity-specific deviation is caused by abnormal pricing of forward rates specific to certain maturities, driven by habitat and preferences of individual and institutional investors.
claims.claim: M arises from abnormal pricing at certain maturities driven by habitat and preferences of individual and institutional investors.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Changes in demand or supply at a given maturity habitat can affect a range of surround- ing maturities — investors treat them as close substitutes — which allows us to treat the maturity-specific deviation as a smooth curve.
claims.claim: Close substitutability across nearby maturities justifies modelling M as a smooth curve.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: a simple yet intuitive model for these deviations would be that they decay towards zero at some rate.
claims.claim: No information on M dynamics, so exponential decay to zero is chosen as the simplest assumption (also needed for HJM no-arbitrage).
claims.exact_rule: exponential decay rate Km for M; HJM requires exponential form

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Given an observed term structure of forward rates that is positive at all maturities, it is possible to find maturity-specific and date-specific deviations that fit the current term structure but produce forecasts of negative forward rates in the future.
claims.claim: The general model can forecast negative forward rates; this is not ruled out a priori.
claims.conditions: not constrained in the fitted model; only HJM checked

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: we employ sums of exponential basis functions for U (τ ) and similar basis functions (that are scaled by Brownian motions) to specify dynamic functional forms for M (τ ; t), and D(τ ; t).
claims.claim: Implementation: U, M and D are sums of exponential basis functions scaled by Brownian-motion-driven states; forward rate is exponentially affine in states.
claims.exact_rule: basis functions exp(-Km tau), exp(-2Km tau), exp(-4Km tau) with state-dependent scaling

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: U 1 (τ ) = C 0 − C 1 e −2K m τ ,
claims.claim: One-factor unconditional curve U1(tau)=C0-C1 exp(-2Km tau) (Eq 6): upward sloping, starts at C0-C1, asymptotes to C0.
claims.exact_rule: U1(tau)=C0 - C1*exp(-2*Km*tau)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: M 1 (τ ; t) = m(t) e −K m τ − e −2K m τ .
claims.claim: One-factor maturity-specific deviation M1(tau;t)=m(t)[exp(-Km tau)-exp(-2Km tau)] (Eq 7), a fixed hump shape scaled by m(t).
claims.exact_rule: M1 = m(t)*(exp(-Km*tau)-exp(-2*Km*tau))

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The precise choice of exponential bases can affect the arbitrage-free status of the model, making it important to verify the HJM conditions for each choice.
claims.claim: Footnote 5: the choice of exponential bases can break no-arbitrage, so the HJM conditions must be checked for each choice.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: the deviation has a humped
claims.claim: One-factor M peaks at tau=ln2/Km and is zero at tau=0 and infinity.
claims.exact_rule: argmax tau of M1 = ln(2)/Km

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: D 1 (τ ; t) = d(t) e −2K m τ .
claims.claim: One-factor date-specific deviation D1=d(t)exp(-2Km tau) (Eq 8): monotone up or down, zero at infinity.
claims.exact_rule: D1(tau;t)=d(t)*exp(-2*Km*tau); d(0)=D1(0;t)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: dm(t) = −m(t)K m dt + γ t dB(t),
claims.claim: State dynamics (Eq 10-11): dm=-Km m dt+gamma dB; dd=-2Km d dt+gamma dB, same diffusion to satisfy HJM.
claims.exact_rule: dm = -Km*m dt + gamma_t dB; dd = -2*Km*d dt + gamma_t dB

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: the maturity-specific curve and the date-specific curve are driven by the same Brownian motion, so that their innovations are perfectly correlated.
claims.claim: One-factor model forces M and D innovations to be perfectly correlated; multi-factor versions are used to avoid this.
claims.conditions: one-factor illustration only; final model has 3 Brownian motions

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: dF 1 (τ ; t) = −K m (2C 1 + m(t))e −2K m (τ ) dt + e −K m (τ ) γ t dB(t).
claims.claim: Forward SDE under one factor (Eq 12), shown to satisfy HJM in Appendix A.1.
claims.exact_rule: dF1 = -Km*(2*C1+m(t))*exp(-2Km tau) dt + exp(-Km tau) gamma_t dB

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: For the period 12/9/1981 to 1/28/2008, we obtain daily prices of all Eurodollar futures con- tracts listed in the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
claims.claim: Data: daily prices of all CME Eurodollar futures contracts 9 Dec 1981 to 28 Jan 2008.
claims.data_needed: CME Eurodollar futures daily prices, all listed contracts

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.claim: Forward rate mapping: price P(tau;t)=100 minus annualised 90-day LIBOR for t+tau to t+tau+90; instantaneous forward at the middle (tau+45) days equals 100-P.
claims.exact_rule: f(tau+45 days; t) = 100 - P(tau;t)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: A typical day would see approximately 40 active contracts, with the maximum being 45. The maturities of the forward rates range from 45 days
claims.claim: Typical day has about 40 contracts (max 45), maturities from 45 days to just over 10 years; training sample averages about 10 contracts out to 4 years.
claims.reported_result: 40 contracts typical, 45 max; training avg ~10 contracts, maturity up to 4 years

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: there are persistent blips in the data for December contracts, perhaps caused by those
claims.claim: December Eurodollar contracts show systematic blips, possibly from swap users; the smooth model cannot fit them.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: In order to build a useful model for prediction, we elected to incorporate these microstructure features into the forecast.
claims.claim: Persistent December-contract microstructure effects are carried forward into the forecast.
claims.exact_rule: see C17 residual carry-forward

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We restricted the alternative models to have no more than 4 Brownian Motions (BMs) that serve as driving state variables.
claims.claim: Candidate set restricted to at most 4 Brownian motions.
claims.exact_rule: max 4 BMs; combinations of arbitrage-free units SM1-SM3
claims.conditions: a larger model set might do better (C15)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: we fit each model over the period 12/09/1981 to 10/28/1991, using daily data from the Eurodollar futures market (2500 days of data).
claims.claim: Model selection training window is 12/09/1981 to 10/28/1991, 2500 days.
claims.exact_rule: training sample = first 2500 trading days
claims.reported_result: 2500 days

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Model 5 obtains the lowest AIC among the 6 candidate models. We therefore chose Model 5 (henceforth CFRS ED model) for empirical implementation reported in the rest of this paper.
claims.claim: AIC picks Model 5 (SM1+SM3) among six candidates.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The CFRS ED model, driven by 3 independent Brownian motions, is the sum of the un- conditional curve, 2 maturity-specific curves, and 4 date-specific curves fitted to 3 exponential
claims.claim: Final model: 3 independent BMs, 1 unconditional curve, 2 maturity-specific and 4 date-specific curves, 3 exponential bases exp(-Km tau), exp(-2Km tau), exp(-4Km tau).
claims.exact_rule: basis {exp(-Km tau), exp(-2Km tau), exp(-4Km tau)}; f=F3+eps (Eq 13-14)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Therefore there are 6 state variables in this system: m 1 (t), m 2 (t), d 1 (t), d 2 (t), d 3 (t) and d 4 (t).
claims.claim: State vector has 6 variables: m1, m2, d1..d4; state-space matrices M, D and drift matrices Vm, Vd are given (Eq 15-16, read from page image).
claims.exact_rule: Vm=diag(-Km,-Km); Vd=diag(-2Km,-2Km,-4Km,-2Km); gamma1^2=(m1+C1)Km^2; gamma2^2=(m2+C1)Km^2/4; gamma3^2=(3 m2+4 C2)2Km^2; u=(C0,0,-C1,-C2)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: it is possible that more extensive forms may perform better than our model in forecast accuracy.
claims.claim: Model set was limited (<=4 BMs); richer forms might forecast better, so results are for one representative member.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: search for a point that maximizes the quasi-likelihood.
claims.claim: Step 1: choose Km and measurement-error variance sigma*^2 by maximising the Kalman quasi-likelihood on all data up to T.
claims.exact_rule: argmax over {Km, sigma*^2} of quasi-ln L using all dates and maturities up to T
claims.data_needed: all Eurodollar forwards up to T

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: to fit the unconditional forward curve of the form: U (τ ) = C 0 − C 1 e −2K m τ − C 2 e −4K m τ
claims.claim: Unconditional curve re-fit at each T on all data to T: U=C0-C1 exp(-2Km tau)-C2 exp(-4Km tau).
claims.exact_rule: refit C0,C1,C2 on all history up to T each forecast date (expanding window)

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Subtract the fitted unconditional forward curve from the observed forward rates to obtain the cross-section of deviations.
claims.claim: Deviations from the fitted U are the Kalman filter observations z_t = f - U.
claims.exact_rule: z_t = f(tau;t) - U_hat(tau) = A x_t + eps_t

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: we evolve these estimates forward according to their respective decay rates to obtain forecasts for future date T 2 :
claims.claim: Forecast: decay each state at its rate: m_i(T2)=m_i(T) exp(-Km (T2-T)); d_1,d_2,d_4 decay at 2Km, d_3 at 4Km.
claims.exact_rule: m_hat(T2)=m_hat(T)*exp(-Km(T2-T)); d1,d2,d4*exp(-2Km(T2-T)); d3*exp(-4Km(T2-T))
claims.direction: forecast forward curve converges to U plus decayed deviations

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Because this microstructure persists in time, our forecast for the future data is
claims.claim: Step 3: add today's cross-sectional fit residual eps(tau+(T2-T);T) to the forecast, treating residuals as persistent microstructure distortion not noise.
claims.exact_rule: f_hat(tau;T2)= smooth forecast + eps(tau+(T2-T);T), i.e. residual at the maturity that will have rolled to tau

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: the imprecise cross-sectional fits are not measurement noise per se, which should dissipate over a longer term, but are market micro-structure distortions that can be expected to persist over the short-term.
claims.claim: Assumption that fit residuals are persistent micro-structure effects.
claims.conditions: over a short term; may not hold at 250 days

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: model selection in section 3.2 uses only data up to 10/28/1991 while forecast generation in section 3.3, uses only the data that is available up to the date that the forecast is being made.
claims.claim: Selection uses data to 28 Oct 1991 only; each forecast uses only data available at its date, so forecasts are out-of-sample (model choice among 6 not re-done).

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: We make forecasts for 5-trading-days, 20-trading-days, 65-trading-days and 250-trading-days ahead, approximately corresponding to 1-calendar-week,
claims.claim: Forecast horizons: 5, 20, 65, 250 trading days (week, month, quarter, year).
claims.exact_rule: horizons 5/20/65/250 trading days

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: the Eurodollar futures prices of each contract remains unchanged over the forecasting period, the random walk model (RW model).
claims.claim: Benchmark: random walk, each contract's price unchanged (forecast change = 0).
claims.exact_rule: RW forecast = current forward rate for each contract

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: For each date, we measure the cross-sectional square root of the mean squared forecast errors (RMSE).
claims.claim: Accuracy metric: cross-sectional RMSE per date, then time-series mean and s.d.; difference tested by Newey-West.
claims.exact_rule: RMSE_t = sqrt(mean over contracts of (forecast - actual forward at end)^2); average over dates

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: The differences in RMSE start from 0.02 basis points (12.53 for the CFRS ED model vs 12.55 for the RW model) for 5-day-ahead forecasts, and monotonically increase to an economically significant 6.31 basis points
claims.claim: RMSE gain over random walk grows with horizon: 0.02 bp at 5 days to 6.31 bp at 250 days.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Panel B of Table 3, shows that the CFRS ED model is consistently more accurate, but the differences are not statistically significant at the usual levels.
claims.claim: RMSE improvements are not statistically significant at any horizon.
claims.reported_result: NW-stat: 5d -0.594, 20d -1.030, 65d -0.365, 250d -0.658 (negative = CFRS better)
claims.conditions: forecast accuracy edge unproven; overlapping windows

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: this structure is very evident in our situation because of the over-lapping forecasting windows.
claims.claim: NW statistic is needed because overlapping forecast windows create serial correlation; footnote 6 also offers Diebold-Mariano.

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine
claims.quote: Each trade signal generated is based on whether the forecasted forward rate is above or below the current Eurodollar-implied forward rate.
claims.claim: Trading rule: forecast forward below current -> short the forward (long the futures); above -> long the forward (short futures); hold to end of forecast period.
claims.exact_rule: signal_i = sign(f_hat(tau;T+h) - f(tau;T)) per contract; long forward (short futures) if >0, short forward (long futures) if <0; hold h days (h=5/20/65/250); all contracts alive at end of period
claims.direction: short forward when model forecasts decline

claims.speaker: Chua, Ramaswamy, Stine

reasoning.question: Can a structural, arbitrage-free model that splits the Eurodollar forward curve into a steady-state curve, decaying preferred-habitat distortions and calendar-date expectation shocks forecast future futures-implied forward rates better than a random walk, and can the forecasts be traded profitably?

thesis.statement: The AIC-selected 3-factor CFRS ED model forecasts Eurodollar forwards slightly better than a random walk at 5-250 day horizons (gains grow with horizon but are not statistically significant), and trading futures in the forecast direction earns 1.2-49bp per trade, only marginally more than always-long buy-and-hold but significantly so on days when the signals differ, especially at 65-250 days.

foundations.premise: The forward curve equals a steady-state curve plus maturity-specific (habitat) and date-specific (expectation) deviations.
foundations.support: preferred habitat (Modigliani-Sutch 1966), expectations hypothesis, equilibrium models (CIR, Vasicek), CFRS (2008)

foundations.premise: Habitat distortions are localized, smooth and decay exponentially to zero at a fixed maturity.
foundations.support: intuition ('simple yet intuitive') plus the HJM no-arbitrage requirement

foundations.premise: Information about future spot rates is tied to calendar dates and rolls toward the short end over time.
The pure expectations hypothesis forecasts worse than a random walk, so only part of the forward curve carries spot-rate information.
The unconditional forward curve slopes upward, so forwards drift down on average (a term premium).
foundations.support: fitted U and the buy-and-hold result

foundations.premise: Cross-sectional misfits (e.g. December contracts) are persistent microstructure distortions, not noise.

mechanism_chain.why: forecasts are more accurate than random walk

reasoning.forward_looking_inputs: (reader) The full Eurodollar (now SOFR) futures strip, decomposed into a long-run average curve, localized humps and calendar-tied expectation shocks, implies expected forward moves over weeks to a year: humps decay at fixed maturities (step 2), expectation shocks roll down (step 3), and the upward-sloping average curve implies a downward drift (step 4). Most of the predictive content at 3-12 months is the term-premium drift; the incremental signal is the model calling rises. It would stop working if the term premium disappears or inverts, in rate regimes unlike the training data, if habitat humps stop decaying (e.g. persistent policy-driven distortions), or once costs on frequent sign changes are counted.
reader_inferences: (reader) Buy-and-hold earns 97-99% of the model's per-trade profit at every horizon, so the strategy is mainly a term-premium carry trade with a small timing overlay.
(reader) The 1991-2008 test period had generally falling rates, which favours always-long futures and downward-drift forecasts.
(reader) The 7.953 NW-stat at 250 days rests on overlapping one-year windows restricted to divergent days, so the effective number of independent observations is small.
(reader) Treating the futures rate as an instantaneous forward ignores convexity, which matters for contracts several years out.
(reader) Nested models with worse likelihood (Table 2) suggest the Kalman QML optimisation may not have converged reliably, which weakens the AIC choice.
(reader) A modern replication would use SOFR futures and OIS forwards, since Eurodollar futures were discontinued in 2023.
(reader) Figure 3 saw-tooth steps occur at the same contracts on all four dates, consistent with persistent contract-specific effects rather than noise.
